I spread the 100 experiments evenly: 20 for each hyperparameter, all as "up" edits. Each block starts from a mid-grid baseline (alpha = 3.59e-05, batch_size = 40, depth = 2, learning_rate_init = 0.00167, width = 101). From there it moves the edited parameter through its low, mid and high bands. It also moves the conditioning parameters one at a time to their extremes. That gives matched pairs, so each possible interaction can be read as a contrast between otherwise identical configurations.

The alpha block focuses on the upper grid values, where L2 is most likely to matter. A few configurations change two parameters at once to check for compound effects.
